newsitem.title: TURKEY: Drop in Turk readyware export value worrisome - TGSD.
newsitem.headline: Drop in Turk readyware export value worrisome - TGSD.

text.p: Turkish clothing manufacturers' association (TGSD) expects readywear exports to increase 20.5 percent to $7.5 billion this year from $6.22 billion in 1996, but a drop in unit values could be worrisome, TGSD chairman Turan Sarigulle said.
"By the end of this year and in the best conditions, our sector's exports may reach $7.5 billion," Sarigulle told a press conference.

"But we shouldn't be so happy about this increase because there are other figures. While our exports rise in quantity, there is a drop in unit value. This is a dangerous signal for the future," Sarigulle said.
According to data released by the Turkish exporters union TIM, readywear exports rose to $3.42 billion in the first six months , up 20 percent from $2.86 billion in the same 1996 period.

But Sarigulle said the industry would face growing difficulty in exporting products with higher added value if productivity was not raised with the help of state support in training, research and development investments.
"Otherwise, our productivity, the main element of international competition will remain far below the levels in other countries," he said.
Total Turkish exports rose to $12.6 billion in January-June 1997, from $10.9 billion in the same period last year. Readywear exports made up 27.1 percent of the total exports in the first half.
Turkey is among the world's top 10 countries in readywear exports and it the second biggest supplier of readwear to the European Union after China.
